item.title: Idea
item.content:encoded:
If you go far enough into the junkyard, you meet not only wild junkbeasts…

… but junkpeople. Civilized junkpeople. Junkpeople who want to communicate with the outside world. Coalition tribes of junkpeople who're part cyborgs from the Steampunk Wars of 1895, and part spontaneous AI emergence from the Great ET Cartridge Dumping of 1983, and they're not too sure what year it is now (surely it can't be past 1920, can it?). Refugees scratching out a living from the leftover energy in fifteen tons of broken solar panels and factory-reject Slinkys.

There's more than one tribe in there, mind you. And not all of them have the same opinion of the outside world. And even the ones who're willing to talk with us peacefully can be pretty damn hard to understand.

The one thing that's clear is that they don't like being stuck inside the junkyard when there's a whole world out there. Some of them want the Foundation to cure them — to make 'normal' again (although we're not sure if those memories were theirs to begin with, or if they're patchworks).

Others want to conquer the rest of the world and bring it all under the sway of the Junkyard God. It's a damn good thing that the anomalous property of the junkyard doesn't extend more than a few meters beyond its borders, so any creature that does manage to get beyond the fences will most likely collapse into inanimate parts. But sufficiently clever planners will take that into account, and there may be ways around it.

Then there are the nihilists. They don't believe there is a world outside the junkyard. Therefore, that the rest of the world does in fact exist… is a huge insult. They don't want to trade with the outside world, they don't want to rejoin the outside world, they don't want to conquer the outside world… they just want to obliterate it. Asking where they'll get more junk if there's no outside world — that's heresy!

And those are just the tribes we understand. Some of them are clearly intelligent. Others are… well, we're not sure if they're people, or animals that happen to act like people. If you've got interchangeable parts, the difference gets blurry.

Hm?

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Cons: I feel that I read about this idea in the d20 Cthulhu book. I am not sure that a 2 meter electric fence is much of a deterrent, nor is 10 guards in junkyard uniforms. Why are they feeding it D class personnel? how does one electromagnetic crane patrol 1.5 km of perimeter? A breach on two fronts would be uncontainable in any case. Flyovers to measure the perimeter? They didn't encounter the red sky? There are other problems as well, but I don't want to grind it down too much.

Pros: …"Extended incursions into SCP-967 have revealed the presence of detritus and derelict vehicles inconsistent with the current level of human technology." This is perhaps the diamond in the rough. Make it a normal junkyard with clutter appearing from different eras, with failing combat cyborgs patching themselves with scrap. The picture is a keeper as well.

I agree with the previous posters, it is very similar to others. Dr Gravity summed it best; "Not bad as first tries go,
I'd suggest taking it down then re-editing it into something more interesting.

And please, please, please use the chat to edit, that's what it's there for."
